claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P on the standard secp256k1 curve, the 32-adding Pollard rho algorithm operating on negation equivalence classes {R,-R} succeeds with exploratory probability at least 0.632 using at most 2^128.000038 total target-group-operation equivalents under the reference price C=78037248 word operations. Peak memory is at most 2^20 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^32 word operations and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success rate relies on the disclosed standard r-adding collision-time heuristic on negation equivalence classes.

experiments.purpose: Verify Pollard rho with negation equivalence classes on toy cyclic additive groups, checking scalar recovery and collision characteristics.
